title: Close AIWorkHub public release and documentation
objective: Prepare the nested tools/geoai-task-mcp repository as the canonical public AIWorkHub release. Audit the complete current worktree against code truth, preserve accepted functionality, remove obsolete public-facing GeoAI/AIWorkingHub naming and legacy runtime instructions, align Python and VS Code extension release versions at 0.6.0, finish concise current documentation, CI/repository hygiene and packaging metadata, and prove the installable VSIX plus repository-local multi-repo/task/callback/tooling workflow. Do not commit or push; Codex owns final publication. This task's transition to review is also the first fresh callback-delivery canary after B857, so finish with normal taskctl review.
acceptance: README begins with what AIWorkHub is, the supported workflow and a five-minute install/init/use path; it reflects current code rather than historical task plans.

Documentation clearly covers VS Code editor-tab dashboard, explicit Init Repo, repository-local .aiworkhub authority, multi-repository isolation, Source Graph, Session Manager, AI Memory, KB, task workers, selected-task Live Output, Codex callback routing and Claude callback capability/limitations.

Linux, Windows, WSL and Remote-SSH installation/operation boundaries are documented without host-specific paths; the obsolete browser dashboard URL and systemd callback requirement are absent from current setup instructions.

Public product/runtime/docs use canonical AIWorkHub naming. Historical fixtures may retain old names only when a test explicitly proves migration compatibility, and such exceptions are documented in the release audit.
Python package and VS Code extension versions are aligned at 0.6.0; package metadata, display names, commands and generated VSIX agree.
MIT license, contribution, security, code-of-conduct, changelog, architecture, getting-started/publishing documentation and useful GitHub issue/PR/CI metadata are coherent and linked from README.

Repository ignores runtime databases, logs, credentials, generated caches and local VSIX artifacts. No secret, repository-local .aiworkhub database, developer absolute path or generated runtime state is selected for publication.
Legacy duplicate Python packages and obsolete service/browser launchers remain removed; current aiworkhub package and VS Code bundled runtime are the only public runtime authority.
The release audit separates production source/docs/tests from historical task/eval artifacts and recommends the smallest safe publication set without deleting potentially valuable history blindly.

All current AIWorkHub-focused Python tests pass, extension JavaScript checks pass, VSIX packages successfully, metadata versions match, git diff check passes, and the exact validation evidence is recorded.
Worker stops at taskctl review with a concise changed-path and validation summary; no commit, push, GitHub rename, release upload or tag is performed by the worker.
validation: cd tools/geoai-task-mcp && PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_aiworkhub_*.py tests/test_repository_state.py tests/test_repository_mux.py tests/test_callback_bridge.py tests/test_process_launcher.py tests/test_process_launcher_security.py tests/test_server_runtime_wiring.py
